problems.cause: Occlusion and alignment errors between focus planes
problems.fix: Retouch from individual source frames; change angle if the overlap is too complex.

problems.cause: Subject or camera moved during capture
problems.fix: Stabilise the setup; do not stack a windblown or moving subject.

problems.cause: Lens focus breathing changes magnification
problems.fix: Leave crop margin and allow alignment; a rail or different lens may help with some setups.

alternatives.name: Fewer frames with more depth each
alternatives.effect: Thicker sharp slices at a slightly smaller aperture.
alternatives.requirements: Same light and ISO; still overlap carefully rather than choosing an arbitrary frame count.

alternatives.name: Landscape focus stack
alternatives.effect: Near foreground and distant scenery combined.
alternatives.requirements: Use a wide lens and only as many overlapping focus distances as the scene needs; avoid moving vegetation.

tip: Keep the source frames. A technically successful automatic stack can still need one clean source to repair a difficult edge.
startingPoint: Make a test frame in the stated light, enlarge the important detail, and adjust before shooting a sequence.

title: Cloud and shadow timelapse
conditions: Clouds and their shadows moving across a static landscape in reasonably steady daylight.
intent: A smooth short sequence that reveals movement too slow to notice in a single photograph.

setup.focusTarget: Focus on a distant landscape detail with magnification, then lock focus for the whole sequence.
setup.whiteBalance: Fixed Daylight or custom balance for the entire sequence
setup.stabilization: Follow camera/lens guidance for fixed tripod work
setup.exposureNote: Start f/8, 1 s, ISO 100, with enough ND for the light and a 3 s start-to-start interval. Keep exposure shorter than the interval with time to write files. About 240 frames make 10 s at 24 fps and take about 12 minutes.

phone.mode: Native time-lapse mode or a manual interval app
phone.iso: Native automatic; lock if the chosen app permits
phone.aperture: Fixed by the selected phone lens; normally not adjustable
phone.shutter: Native automatic; manual target about 1 s with 3 s intervals
phone.focus: Lock focus on the static landscape
phone.focal: Main lens fixed throughout the sequence
phone.whiteBalance: Auto; lock white balance for a series only if the app supports it.
phone.guidance: Secure the phone, check battery and capture a short test before a long run.
phone.limitation: Native time-lapse often chooses intervals and exposure automatically; true slow shutters may require an app and ND.
why: A fixed phone position lets cloud movement remain the only large change between frames.
Native time-lapse modes often choose timing automatically, so output duration cannot be promised from the camera recipe.
A manual interval sequence needs exposure plus file-writing time to fit inside each start-to-start interval.
steps: Choose a stable landscape view with moving clouds, secure the phone and check battery, storage and weather protection.
Select native Time-lapse for an automatic sequence, or a documented interval app for separately saved frames.
Keep one lens selected and lock focus/exposure/WB where the app supports it; make a short playback test.
For a manual example, use a supported exposure around 1 s and 3 s start-to-start intervals; suitable physical ND may be needed in daylight because aperture is fixed.
Record about 240 manual frames for roughly 10 s at 24 fps, taking about 12 minutes at that interval; native timing may differ.
Inspect playback for flicker, shake and missing frames before committing to a longer run, and retain source images when the app provides them.

optional: Manual interval app for timing control
Compatible ND filter for true slow exposures

problems.cause: The phone or support moved.
problems.fix: Use a rigid sheltered mount and avoid touching the setup during recording.

problems.cause: Automatic exposure/WB changed between frames.
problems.fix: Use supported locks or more consistent light; gradual day-to-night changes need a deliberately managed workflow.

problems.cause: Interval, exposure or processing demands exceeded capture capability.
problems.fix: Shorten exposure or lengthen the interval in a manual app and test writing time.

problems.symptom: Final duration differs from the planned frame calculation
problems.cause: The native mode selected its own interval or playback processing.
problems.fix: Accept its automatic result or use a documented manual interval workflow for exact counts.

phone.tip: Play back a short test before the long wait; timing and flicker problems are easier to fix at the start.

why: A 1 s exposure blurs some cloud movement within each 3 s capture interval.
Locked exposure, focus and white balance reduce brightness and colour flicker in steady light.
The capture interval, not playback fps alone, determines the motion jump between frames.
steps: Choose clouds moving across a fixed foreground and allow room for video cropping.
Secure the tripod against wind without adding swinging weight.
Set manual exposure, fixed balance and focus; use ND for the intended 1 s shutter.
Program a 3 s start-to-start interval and confirm the camera’s interval definition.
Shoot a short test sequence and check dropped frames, clipping and movement.
Capture the full run, then assemble at 24 fps and inspect for flicker or alignment shifts.

optional: External power approved for the camera

problems.cause: Automatic settings, changing aperture actuation or unstable light
problems.fix: Lock settings in steady light; use supported exposure smoothing or later deflicker for genuine light transitions.

problems.cause: Exposure plus processing exceeds interval
problems.fix: Shorten shutter, lengthen the interval or disable processing that doubles capture time.

problems.cause: Interval is long relative to cloud speed
problems.fix: Try 1–2 s start-to-start intervals or add appropriate exposure blur.

problems.cause: Tripod moves or stabilization shifts framing
problems.fix: Stabilise the support and follow manufacturer guidance for tripod stabilization.

alternatives.name: Fast clouds
alternatives.effect: More frequent samples with less movement per frame.
alternatives.requirements: Use a 1.5–2 s interval; adjust ND one stop lighter than base for equal brightness.

alternatives.name: Slow cloud build-up
alternatives.effect: Longer blur and a more accelerated passage of time.
alternatives.requirements: Use a 5 s interval and one extra stop of ND relative to the base.

tip: For a sunrise or sunset with large brightness changes, use a planned exposure ramp; the fixed-exposure daylight recipe will not cover the whole transition.
startingPoint: Make a test frame in the stated light, enlarge the important detail, and adjust before shooting a sequence.

title: Stroboscopic flash motion sequence
conditions: A light-coloured ball or small object moving along a controlled path against a dark background in a darkened room.
intent: Several separately frozen positions of the same moving object inside one photograph.

setup.focusTarget: Place the object at the planned movement plane, focus with magnification, then lock manual focus before darkening the room.
setup.whiteBalance: Flash or a fixed custom balance under the actual light
setup.stabilization: Follow lens guidance for a locked tripod
setup.metering: Make a no-flash test for ambient, then inspect flash-lit copies
setup.exposureNote: Start f/8, 2 s, ISO 200 with MULTI/RPT flash set to 8 pulses at 4 Hz and about 1/32 power, within the flash’s stated limits. The 2 s window covers 8 ÷ 4; adjust pulse output or distance for brightness, frequency for spacing.

phone.mode: Documented true long exposure with independent repeating light, or ordinary burst plus a labelled multi-image composite
phone.iso: Lowest practical fixed ISO for a supported long exposure; automatic or suitable manual ISO for burst originals
phone.aperture: Fixed by the selected phone lens; normally not adjustable
phone.shutter: True 2–3 s only if genuinely supported; otherwise separate short burst exposures for a composite
phone.focus: Pre-focus on the movement plane and lock it
phone.focal: Main lens on a secure support
phone.whiteBalance: Fixed balance matched to the repeating or continuous light if selectable; otherwise Auto.
phone.guidance: Test a true continuous exposure with independent repeating light, or combine separately saved sharp burst frames as an explicitly labelled composite.
phone.limitation: Native phone flash systems generally do not provide programmable pulse count, power and frequency; night-mode stacking can reject or merge the repeated positions.
why: The phone’s built-in flash is not assumed to provide programmable pulse count, frequency or output.
A true long exposure can record an independently controlled repeating light only when the phone/app genuinely supports that exposure.
A burst of separate sharp images can make a related composite result, but it must be identified as a composite rather than one stroboscopic capture.
steps: Choose a small light-coloured object and a controlled clear path; warn nearby people about flashing light and avoid it around anyone sensitive to flashes.
Mount the phone and lock focus on the movement plane. Test whether the app records one true 2–3 s exposure rather than a Night stack.

For the single-exposure route, darken ambient light and use an independently controlled compatible repeating flash within its manual’s limits; 8 pulses at 4 Hz take about 2 s, with capture margin needed for trigger timing.
Start at low permitted flash output and the phone’s lowest practical ISO; test timing and brightness before moving the object, adjusting external flash output or distance separately.
If that setup is unavailable, use bright continuous light and an ordinary short-exposure burst, save the separate originals and combine 3–6 clear positions with masks in a layer editor.
Inspect each position for blur, clipping and overlap; retain originals and clearly distinguish the one-exposure result from the multi-image composite.

essential: Either documented true-long-exposure capture plus independent programmable repeating light, or a burst-export and layer-editing workflow
optional: Continuous light for the composite alternative

problems.symptom: Phone offers no pulse count or frequency setting
problems.cause: Its built-in flash lacks programmable repeating control.
problems.fix: Use a separately controlled compatible system or the ordinary-burst composite alternative.

problems.symptom: Repeated positions disappear or merge unexpectedly
problems.cause: The app used computational Night processing instead of one continuous exposure.
problems.fix: Verify true exposure support, or save separate short burst frames and build a labelled composite.

problems.symptom: A continuous ghost joins all the positions
problems.cause: Ambient light recorded the moving object between flash pulses.
problems.fix: Reduce ambient for the single-exposure route; for a composite choose sharper originals and cleaner masks.

problems.symptom: Positions overlap or become too bright
problems.cause: Pulse spacing is too tight, flash output excessive or the same area accumulated light.
problems.fix: Reduce external flash frequency/output or change distance within equipment limits; in a composite select fewer separated positions and adjust blending.

phone.tip: Test a stationary object for brightness first, then test timing; changing both at once makes the cause of a failure unclear.
phone.conditions: A light-coloured object on a controlled path: a darkened room for a verified continuous exposure with independent repeating light, or bright steady light for separate burst originals.
phone.intent: Show several distinct object positions through a verified repeating-light exposure or an explicitly labelled composite of separate sharp frames.

why: Repeated short flash pulses record separate positions while the shutter remains open.
A dark background and low ambient light prevent a continuous blur from filling the gaps.
Flash frequency and object speed control spacing; the camera shutter must cover the complete programmed pulse sequence.
steps: Set a safe repeatable object path in front of a dark background; keep people and fragile objects clear.
Mount the camera and pre-focus on a stationary object at the movement plane, then lock focus.
Choose M, f/8, ISO 200 and 2 s; take a no-flash test that should be almost black.
On a compatible flash select MULTI/RPT, 8 flashes, 4 Hz and about 1/32 power; confirm the flash manual permits this combination.
Start the controlled movement and exposure together, using a helper or suitable remote trigger.
Inspect position spacing, brightness and missed pulses; adjust frequency for spacing and flash power or distance for brightness.

essential: Flash supporting programmable repeating / MULTI mode

problems.symptom: Positions merge into a bright smear
problems.cause: Too much ambient light or pulses too closely spaced
problems.fix: Darken the room first; then lower flash frequency or increase object travel between pulses.

problems.cause: Shutter closes too soon or flash cannot sustain the selected burst
problems.fix: Use at least flash count ÷ frequency for the exposure window; reduce power/count and check the flash’s repeating-mode limits.

problems.symptom: All object copies are too dark
problems.cause: Low pulse output or excessive flash distance
problems.fix: Move the flash closer or increase supported pulse power; changing shutter alone does not brighten each flash-lit copy.

problems.symptom: Each copy is soft despite distinct spacing
problems.cause: Wrong focus plane or a pulse too long to freeze the object
problems.fix: Keep motion in the prefocused plane and use lower flash power with the flash closer if the system permits.

alternatives.name: Four widely spaced positions
alternatives.effect: Fewer, clearer stages of the movement.
alternatives.requirements: Set 4 flashes at 2 Hz, start near 1/32 power and keep the subject speed similar; confirm supported flash settings.

alternatives.name: Finer eight-position sampling
alternatives.effect: More closely spaced stages over a shorter part of the path.
alternatives.requirements: Set 8 flashes at 8 Hz with supported low output; copies may overlap unless the object moves farther between pulses.

tip: Move the object across the frame at roughly constant speed for even spacing; changing spacing can then reveal acceleration.
startingPoint: Test the full pulse sequence, then inspect every frozen position; flash output, movement speed and room darkness determine the result.
safety: Warn everyone present before using repeating flashes; avoid use around people sensitive to flashing light or around animals. Follow the flash manufacturer’s burst and cooling limits.
